post.summary: Add a transaction, a transfer or a split
post.description: On-budget accounts: a null category means Uncategorized; credit-card payment categories can't be used. Tracking accounts never have a category. The payee is matched by name (ignoring case) and created if new; null leaves it empty. `transferAccountId` (instead of `payeeName`) makes it a transfer: a matching transaction with the opposite amount is kept in that account. Only a transfer from a budget account to a tracking account has a category (on the budget side), as money leaves the budget. New transfers need both accounts open. `subtransactions` (two or more lines, adding up to the amount) splits it across categories; its own `categoryId` is then null. Lines follow the same category and transfer rules. Only budget accounts have splits, and a transfer can't be split (its lines can be transfers).

400.description: Invalid input, a closed account, a category the account can't use, or a transfer to the same account

403.description: The caller's role can't change transactions

404.description: No such budget, account or transaction, or the caller isn't a member

patch.summary: Edit a transaction, move it to another account, or toggle cleared
patch.description: On-budget accounts: a null category means Uncategorized; credit-card payment categories can't be used. Tracking accounts never have a category. The payee is matched by name (ignoring case) and created if new; null leaves it empty. `transferAccountId` (instead of `payeeName`) makes it a transfer: a matching transaction with the opposite amount is kept in that account. Only a transfer from a budget account to a tracking account has a category (on the budget side), as money leaves the budget. New transfers need both accounts open. On a transfer, date and amount changes apply to both sides; memo, cleared, flag and category are per side. Setting `payeeName` turns a transfer back into a normal transaction and deletes the other side. Setting `cleared` on a reconciled transaction unlocks it. Moving it to an account that can't use its category resets the category. `subtransactions` (two or more lines, adding up to the amount) splits it across categories; its own `categoryId` is then null. Lines follow the same category and transfer rules. Only budget accounts have splits, and a transfer can't be split (its lines can be transfers). Sending `subtransactions` replaces a split's lines (matched by `id`); changing a split's amount needs new lines too. Giving a split a `categoryId` (or making it a transfer) un-splits it. A split's transfer side only takes memo, cleared, flag and category.
